scientific_question: How does the specified visible-light reaction of buta-1,3-diene, sodium difluoromethanesulfinate and methyl 2,3,4,5,6-pentafluorobenzoate form the observed polyfluoroaryl sulfones, and what governs its 1,4-versus-1,2 regiochemical competition and E/Z product preference, including the switch to preferential 1,2 addition for (1E)-1-phenylbuta-1,3-diene under its specified related conditions?

inputs.content: Sodium difluoromethanesulfinate: CHF2-S(=O)-O(-), with a sodium counterion. The carbon bears one hydrogen and two fluorines.
Methyl 2,3,4,5,6-pentafluorobenzoate: a benzene ring bearing C(=O)OCH3 at one carbon and fluorine at each of the other five ring carbons.

Butadiene system: buta-1,3-diene 1.0 mmol (5.0 equivalents), supplied as 0.50 mL of a 2.0 mol L^-1 solution in THF, sodium difluoromethanesulfinate 0.6 mmol (3.0 equivalents), methyl 2,3,4,5,6-pentafluorobenzoate 0.2 mmol (1.0 equivalent), 4CzIPN photocatalyst 1.5 mol%, ZnCl2 1.0 equivalent, Na2CO3 2.0 equivalents, dry DMSO 1.5 mL, 30 °C, 5 W blue LEDs, 48 h, nitrogen atmosphere. Phenyl-diene comparison: (1E)-1-phenylbuta-1,3-diene 0.3 mmol (1.5 equivalents), sodium difluoromethanesulfinate 0.6 mmol (3.0 equivalents), the same methyl pentafluorobenzoate 0.2 mmol (1.0 equivalent), 4CzIPN 1.5 mol%, ZnCl2 1.0 equivalent, dry DMF 2.0 mL, 30 °C, 40 W blue LEDs, 48 h, nitrogen atmosphere; no added carbonate base in these comparison conditions. 4CzIPN denotes 2,4,5,6-tetrakis(9H-carbazol-9-yl)benzene-1,3-dicarbonitrile. Equivalents and isolated yields are relative to the methyl pentafluorobenzoate.

The butadiene system gives predominantly the 1,4-addition sulfone methyl (E)-4-[(5,5-difluoropent-2-en-1-yl)sulfonyl]-2,3,5,6-tetrafluorobenzoate, with isolated yield 74%; its Z alkene isomer has isolated yield 7%. Their shared connectivity is Ar-S(=O)2-CH2-CH=CH-CH2-CHF2, where Ar is the methyl-benzoate ring bearing sulfur para to C(=O)OCH3 and fluorine at ring positions 2,3,5,6. No 1,2-addition byproduct was detected in this butadiene comparison; no detection limit is supplied.

The phenyl-substituted comparison is (1E)-1-phenylbuta-1,3-diene: Ph-CH=CH-CH=CH2, with Ph an unsubstituted phenyl group and E geometry at the phenyl-side double bond. Phenyl is attached to a terminal diene carbon, not an internal carbon.

The specified phenyl-diene comparison preferentially gives the 1,2-addition sulfone methyl (E)-4-[(5,5-difluoro-1-phenylpent-1-en-3-yl)sulfonyl]-2,3,5,6-tetrafluorobenzoate, isolated yield 74%. Its connectivity is Ph-CH=CH-CH[S(=O)2-Ar]-CH2-CHF2, with E geometry at Ph-CH=CH and the same tetrafluorinated methyl-benzoate Ar group as in the butadiene products. No quantitative competing-product detection limit or enantioselectivity measurement is supplied for this representative comparison; do not infer an absolute configuration at the sulfur-bearing carbon.
